clusters.state_of_play: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has signed an executive order imposing the first statewide moratorium on new large (hyperscaler) data centers for one year, citing energy grid, environmental, and ratepayer cost concerns, including ensuring New Yorkers do not bear costs of transmission and infrastructure build-outs, while state lawmakers draft a nation-leading regulatory framework. The moratorium is drawing backlash from critics who say it will further damage upstate New York's already sagging economy. President Trump has publicly blasted the moratorium, demanding Hochul reverse the policy immediately. The action follows a growing left-wing grassroots campaign, backed by Sanders-aligned progressives, opposing AI data center expansion. Similar grassroots opposition is emerging elsewhere, including Paulding County, Georgia, where furious homeowners packed standing-room-only county commission meetings and held a protest demanding a local moratorium, and in Florida, where residents near a proposed hyperscale data center in Trump's backyard are fuming over water supply risks despite the project's claim of generating over $500 million in annual tax revenue. Opposition to AI data centers is emerging as one of the rare cross-partisan political issues of the cycle. Separately, a PJM power auction covering the nation's largest electrical grid is projected to add $6.3 billion in additional charges to consumers and businesses across 13 states as a direct result of data center electricity demand. Axios has framed Hochul's moratorium as a replicable Democratic playbook for other governors ahead of the 2026 midterms.

clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. On Wednesday, Trump's CDC director nominee Erica Schwartz faced Senate confirmation, vowing to 'never betray the science' and pledge 'radical transparency,' but struggled to convince senators she would stand up to RFK Jr. Separately, Trump's health emergency preparedness nominee Sean Kaufman walked back past comments skeptical of Covid-19 and hepatitis B vaccine safety, drawing a heated exchange with Sen. Cassidy. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries, and health workers in Ituri province have separately begun striking over unpaid wages. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. CDC travel restrictions have been extended to also cover some travelers from Uganda and South Sudan. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: The UK and EU have signed a post-Brexit Gibraltar treaty at a Brussels ceremony, removing the land border between Gibraltar and Spain and allowing Gibraltar residents to cross using residence cards and Spanish citizens using government ID. The treaty came into effect at midnight, accompanied by a symbolic ceremony and large crowds crossing freely. The old chain-link border fence has been physically torn down, Spanish border checks have been relocated to the international airport and seaport, and Gibraltar is in effect becoming part of the Schengen zone via the EU entry system. Brits entering Gibraltar from Spain will now be fingerprinted under the new arrangements. Tory and Reform MPs are warning this represents a foreign policy 'betrayal' and that Falklands sovereignty could be Labour's next concession. Andy Burnham has secured 349 Labour MP nominations — including all eligible cabinet members — making it impossible for any rival to challenge him, and is confirmed as Britain's next Prime Minister, expected to take office on 20 July. Burnham has pledged a 'broad church' cabinet and party culture, is considering a larger autumn Budget with allies lobbying for a land tax, public control of utilities and expanded devolution. A new Real Rates Reform Alliance is now also pressing him to go further on business rates reform, calling for a 2% online sales tax to fund a 37% cut in rates for physical retailers. He plans to scrap David Lammy's jury-trial abolition proposals. He voted to back immigration curbs at the Immigration and Asylum Bill's second reading despite a threatened left-wing revolt. Burnham has not uttered a word in the Commons chamber since being sworn in as Makerfield MP on 22 June. Tories are demanding Parliament delay its summer recess to scrutinise him before he takes office. The Reform UK/Farage financial scrutiny story continues: the £5m crypto donor is now linked to Tether, a giant and secretive cryptocurrency firm that Farage has publicly championed. Separately, Farage refused taxpayer-funded security as inadequate, with Reform UK continuing to fund his personal protection.

US strikes have hit port cities of Bushehr and Bandar Abbas, as well as a 90-minute attack on Iran's Greater Tunb Island targeting cruise missile storage and launch sites. US attacks have killed dozens in Iran, pushing a fragile ceasefire closer to collapse. A Situation Room meeting was held to plan a wider offensive broader in scope than the current Strait of Hormuz campaign. Trump warned strikes would intensify next week if Iran does not cooperate in peace talks, while also calling off a previously announced 20% fee on Hormuz shipping, replacing it with investment and trade deals with Gulf Arab states. Iran claims to have destroyed the US Fifth Fleet command centre and targeted a US naval support base in Bahrain's capital, with sirens reported in Manama. clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. On Wednesday, Trump's CDC director nominee Erica Schwartz faced Senate confirmation, vowing to 'never betray the science' and pledge 'radical transparency,' but struggled to convince senators she would stand up to RFK Jr. Separately, Trump's health emergency preparedness nominee Sean Kaufman walked back past comments skeptical of Covid-19 and hepatitis B vaccine safety, drawing a heated exchange with Sen. Cassidy. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries, and health workers in Ituri province have separately begun striking over unpaid wages. British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. In the UK, major incidents have been declared in North Wales and in Glossop, Derbyshire in the Peak District, with at least 10 wildfires burning across Wales and 19 separate wildfires being tackled across the UK overall. A wildfire near Conwy Mountain prompted evacuation of 36 homes. A 20-year-old woman, Shania Care-Slede, has been charged with aggravated arson in connection with a UK moor fire for which a major incident was declared. The Met Office's Fire Severity Index identifies parts of southern England — including around Chichester and Bognor Regis in West Sussex — as most at risk. clusters.state_of_play: China and North Korea are marking the 65th anniversary of their friendship treaty. North Korean Premier Pak Thae-song traveled to Beijing, met with Xi Jinping, and Kim Jong-un and Xi exchanged messages pledging deeper strategic cooperation. South Korea has separately voiced concern that North Korean actions along the DMZ constitute a breach of the 1953 armistice agreement. In a related development, China has put Chinese-born American seismologist Youlin Chen on trial after nearly two years of detention; Chen published US-funded research on detecting North Korean nuclear tests and worked as a US government contractor for the State Department and Air Force Research Lab. China's foreign ministry has rejected claims of 'wrongful detention' while not denying that Chen is imprisoned. Chen's wife Yufang Rong is publicly appealing to Trump to help bring him home. New reporting reveals that Trump made a direct personal appeal to Xi Jinping for Chen's release, which went unanswered. Separately, a major Iranian newspaper has published a threat of retaliation against German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, drawing concern from German politicians and a cautious response from the German government. In technology and finance developments: CXMT, China's leading memory chip maker and a linchpin of its AI ambitions, is planning a ~$10B IPO in Shanghai. Oracle is leading a bid to supply Japan with air-gapped top-secret cloud services, under US pressure on Tokyo to tighten data security. Japan's government bond market is selling off amid policy normalization and fiscal concerns, with some experts flagging renewed investor opportunity. Satellite images have revealed that China has constructed a full-scale replica of a US Navy destroyer in the Taklamakan Desert, suggesting active target practice or weapons testing against US naval hardware profiles. In London, Metropolitan Police are investigating Chinese embassy guards for allegedly brandishing cattle prods at protestors, while a High Court legal challenge has begun over China's plans for a large new embassy building. clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. On Wednesday, Trump's CDC director nominee Erica Schwartz faced Senate confirmation, vowing to 'never betray the science' and pledge 'radical transparency,' but struggled to convince senators she would stand up to RFK Jr. Separately, Trump's health emergency preparedness nominee Sean Kaufman walked back past comments skeptical of Covid-19 and hepatitis B vaccine safety, drawing a heated exchange with Sen. Cassidy. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries, and health workers in Ituri province have separately begun striking over unpaid wages. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. CDC travel restrictions have been extended to also cover some travelers from Uganda and South Sudan. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. On Wednesday, Trump's CDC director nominee Erica Schwartz faced Senate confirmation, vowing to 'never betray the science' and pledge 'radical transparency,' but struggled to convince senators she would stand up to RFK Jr. Separately, Trump's health emergency preparedness nominee Sean Kaufman walked back past comments skeptical of Covid-19 and hepatitis B vaccine safety, drawing a heated exchange with Sen. Cassidy. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries, and health workers in Ituri province have separately begun striking over unpaid wages. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. CDC travel restrictions have been extended to also cover some travelers from Uganda and South Sudan. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: Missouri has declared a state of emergency in response to severe storms and flash flooding described as once-in-a-millennium rainfall; Governor Mike Kehoe activated the state emergency operations center. At least one person has died — identified as Faith Gregory of Crawford County, whose home was swept from its foundation and whose body was found by volunteers late Saturday. More than 202 children and staff were airlifted by Missouri National Guard Black Hawk helicopters from Camp Taum Sauk in Lesterville after nearby roads were washed away. Around 20 people who climbed to the roof of a collapsed building at the Barecat Getaway campground in Reynolds County were also airlifted to safety. Some campers climbed into trees to escape rising waters, prompting a state mutual aid request. Up to a foot of rain fell overnight in southeastern Missouri, prompting more than 350 rescues from floodwaters overall. More than 20 million people across at least 14 states from Colorado to Pennsylvania are under flood watches through Saturday. The flash-flood threat is continuing into Sunday, extending from Tennessee to West Virginia. The threat has expanded significantly in Texas: a state of emergency has been declared covering nearly 60 counties, a flash flood emergency has been triggered in Central Texas, more than a foot of rain has fallen in parts of Texas in 24 hours leading to dozens of rescues, highways have been washed out, and motorists have been stranded. A tornado was spawned in San Antonio. Kerr County officials — site of last year's Camp Mystic disaster that killed 28 people — are in contact with summer camps now at risk. Forecasters warn of isolated totals of up to 15 inches possible. Camp Mystic operators have moved five lawsuits filed by families over last year's catastrophic flooding to federal court, citing bankruptcy. A heat dome is simultaneously driving triple-digit temperatures from Southern California to the Northeast, threatening record-breaking heat. Separately, days of torrential monsoon rain have triggered major flooding in Bangladesh, killing at least 51 people and leaving millions stranded in the south-east of the country, with food supply shortages reported. On the immigration enforcement front: a Venezuelan man (Jesús Manuel Arenas-Silva, 45) died in ICE custody in Georgia, becoming the 22nd such death this year. A 28-year-old man fleeing ICE agents in St. Augustine, Florida was struck and killed by a tractor-trailer, the third death in a week involving ICE encounters following fatal shootings of two men during vehicle stops in Maine and Texas six days apart. In response, ICE has suspended most vehicle stops.

items.title: UK hit by widespread ‘firewave’ as wildfire risk grows, experts warn

ledger.what_new: 19 separate wildfires being tackled across the UK, per officials.
ledger.unique: Specific updated count of 19 active UK wildfires from official source.

clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with nationality now confirmed: five Britons, three Belgians, one French national, and one Spanish national among the dead; DNA identification was required for badly burned victims. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. In the UK, major incidents have been declared in North Wales and in Glossop, Derbyshire in the Peak District, with at least 10 wildfires burning across Wales and 19 separate wildfires being tackled across the UK overall. A wildfire near Conwy Mountain prompted evacuation of 36 homes. A 20-year-old woman, Shania Care-Slede, has been charged with aggravated arson in connection with a UK moor fire for which a major incident was declared. The Met Office's Fire Severity Index identifies parts of southern England — including around Chichester and Bognor Regis in West Sussex — as most at risk. An 'exceptional' wildfire warning has been issued for parts of the UK as a heatwave, now entering its second week in some areas, is forecast to last at least another week; hosepipe bans are in effect. The National Fire Chiefs Council warned that hot dry weather 'significantly increases wildfire risk.' Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.' In a separate legal development, Sánchez's brother David has been banned from holding public office for nine years after being convicted of administrative misconduct relating to his hiring by a socialist-led council in Extremadura.

clusters.state_of_play: Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-SC) died Saturday at age 71 from a heart attack. President Trump publicly recommended that South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster appoint Graham's sister, Darline Graham Nordone, calling it a 'fabulous tribute,' and Sen. Tim Scott is also pushing for her appointment. Darline spoke briefly with the New York Post about the loss of her brother. McMaster is expected to announce his pick at a press conference. A White House plan is reportedly in place to avoid appointing Rep. Nancy Mace, and at least one Fox News figure has withdrawn from contention. Republicans in South Carolina have begun jockeying for the full six-year Senate seat election separate from the caretaker appointment. Ukraine is grappling with the loss of a key Trump-orbit ally. Social media has seen false claims of criminal action in Graham's death, a California nurse who pre-death wished harm on Graham and Trump, and comedian Margaret Cho's viral video mocking Graham's death. South Carolina lawmakers including Tim Scott, Nancy Mace, William Timmons, and Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette paid tribute. On The View, Sunny Hostin said Graham 'betrayed his country for power' while Ana Navarro condemned those celebrating his death. Graham had become Darline's legal guardian after their parents died 15 months apart and called her the closest person in his life.

clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. On Wednesday, Trump's CDC director nominee Erica Schwartz faced Senate confirmation, vowing to 'never betray the science' and pledge 'radical transparency,' but struggled to convince senators she would stand up to RFK Jr. Separately, Trump's health emergency preparedness nominee Sean Kaufman walked back past comments skeptical of Covid-19 and hepatitis B vaccine safety, drawing a heated exchange with Sen. Cassidy. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with nationality now confirmed: five Britons, three Belgians, one French national, and one Spanish national among the dead; DNA identification was required for badly burned victims. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. In the UK, major incidents have been declared in North Wales and in Glossop, Derbyshire in the Peak District, with at least 10 wildfires burning across Wales and 19 separate wildfires being tackled across the UK overall. A wildfire near Conwy Mountain prompted evacuation of 36 homes. A 20-year-old woman, Shania Care-Slede, has been charged with aggravated arson in connection with a UK moor fire for which a major incident was declared. The Met Office's Fire Severity Index identifies parts of southern England — including around Chichester and Bognor Regis in West Sussex — as most at risk. An 'exceptional' wildfire warning has been issued for parts of the UK as a heatwave, now entering its second week in some areas, is forecast to last at least another week; hosepipe bans are in effect. The National Fire Chiefs Council warned that hot dry weather 'significantly increases wildfire risk.' Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.' In a separate legal development, Sánchez's brother David has been banned from holding public office for nine years after being convicted of administrative misconduct relating to his hiring by a socialist-led council in Extremadura.

clusters.state_of_play: Inflation cooled more than expected in June, with annual CPI hitting 3.5% (beating the 3.8% forecast), driven by falling gas prices; month-over-month prices posted their biggest drop since 2020. New York Fed President John Williams stated that inflation has peaked and rates are "well positioned," citing five reasons why the latest price surge has run its course. However, gas prices remain 70 cents per gallon above last year, and real wage gains since Trump took office amount to just 27 cents per hour, as June's 3.5% wage growth was entirely offset by 3.5% inflation. Trump's net approval on inflation has collapsed to minus 50, worse than Biden and Carter. Renewed Iran conflict threatens to push energy costs and inflation back up, and many household costs remain stubbornly high. Additionally, beef prices continue to climb due to drought, historically low herd sizes, and fears over the new world screwworm parasite entering the US, with Texas business owners warning that passing costs to consumers risks losing customers.

clusters.state_of_play: China and North Korea are marking the 65th anniversary of their friendship treaty. North Korean Premier Pak Thae-song traveled to Beijing, met with Xi Jinping, and Kim Jong-un and Xi exchanged messages pledging deeper strategic cooperation. Separately, Kim Jong-un convened a rare military commission meeting where he denounced corruption in the military, announced plans to boost North Korea's nuclear force in quality and quantity, and ordered a radical expansion of espionage activities targeting South Korea. South Korea has separately voiced concern that North Korean actions along the DMZ constitute a breach of the 1953 armistice agreement. In a related development, China has put Chinese-born American seismologist Youlin Chen on trial after nearly two years of detention; Chen published US-funded research on detecting North Korean nuclear tests and worked as a US government contractor for the State Department and Air Force Research Lab. China's foreign ministry has rejected claims of 'wrongful detention' while not denying that Chen is imprisoned. Chen's wife Yufang Rong is publicly appealing to Trump to help bring him home. New reporting reveals that Trump made a direct personal appeal to Xi Jinping for Chen's release, which went unanswered. Separately, a major Iranian newspaper has published a threat of retaliation against German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, drawing concern from German politicians and a cautious response from the German government. In technology and finance developments: CXMT, China's leading memory chip maker and a linchpin of its AI ambitions, is planning a ~$10B IPO in Shanghai. Oracle is leading a bid to supply Japan with air-gapped top-secret cloud services, under US pressure on Tokyo to tighten data security. Japan's government bond market is selling off amid policy normalization and fiscal concerns, with some experts flagging renewed investor opportunity. Satellite images have revealed that China has constructed a full-scale replica of a US Navy destroyer in the Taklamakan Desert, suggesting active target practice or weapons testing against US naval hardware profiles. A US airstrike on Feb. 28 killed approximately 200 people, mostly schoolchildren, at the Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab, Iran; the Pentagon's investigation findings remain withheld, with Democratic senators led by Kirsten Gillibrand demanding release within one week, while Trump has shrugged off the incident and the US officially has not accepted responsibility. In London, Metropolitan Police are investigating Chinese embassy guards for allegedly brandishing cattle prods at protestors, while a High Court legal challenge has begun over China's plans for a large new embassy building. A new Pew Research Center survey finds that more countries around the world now favour China over the US, and that global confidence in Xi Jinping exceeds that in Donald Trump.

items.title: Parasitic infection outbreak exposes deep cracks in public health

clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. On Wednesday, Trump's CDC director nominee Erica Schwartz faced Senate confirmation, vowing to 'never betray the science' and pledge 'radical transparency,' but struggled to convince senators she would stand up to RFK Jr. Separately, Trump's health emergency preparedness nominee Sean Kaufman walked back past comments skeptical of Covid-19 and hepatitis B vaccine safety, drawing a heated exchange with Sen. Cassidy. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries, and health workers in Ituri province have separately begun striking over unpaid wages. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. CDC travel restrictions have been extended to also cover some travelers from Uganda and South Sudan. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has signed an executive order imposing the first statewide moratorium on new large (hyperscaler) data centers for one year, citing energy grid, environmental, and ratepayer cost concerns, including ensuring New Yorkers do not bear costs of transmission and infrastructure build-outs, while state lawmakers draft a nation-leading regulatory framework. The moratorium is drawing backlash from critics who say it will further damage upstate New York's already sagging economy. President Trump has publicly blasted the moratorium, demanding Hochul reverse the policy immediately. The action follows a growing left-wing grassroots campaign, backed by Sanders-aligned progressives, opposing AI data center expansion. Similar grassroots opposition is emerging elsewhere, including Paulding County, Georgia, where furious homeowners packed standing-room-only county commission meetings and held a protest demanding a local moratorium, and in Florida, where residents near a proposed hyperscale data center in Trump's backyard are fuming over water supply risks despite the project's claim of generating over $500 million in annual tax revenue. Opposition to AI data centers is emerging as one of the rare cross-partisan political issues of the cycle. Separately, a PJM power auction covering the nation's largest electrical grid is projected to add $6.3 billion in additional charges to consumers and businesses across 13 states as a direct result of data center electricity demand. Axios has framed Hochul's moratorium as a replicable Democratic playbook for other governors ahead of the 2026 midterms.

clusters.state_of_play: Missouri has declared a state of emergency in response to severe storms and flash flooding described as once-in-a-millennium rainfall; Governor Mike Kehoe activated the state emergency operations center. At least one person has died — identified as Faith Gregory of Crawford County, whose home was swept from its foundation and whose body was found by volunteers late Saturday. More than 202 children and staff were airlifted by Missouri National Guard Black Hawk helicopters from Camp Taum Sauk in Lesterville after nearby roads were washed away. Around 20 people who climbed to the roof of a collapsed building at the Barecat Getaway campground in Reynolds County were also airlifted to safety. Some campers climbed into trees to escape rising waters, prompting a state mutual aid request. Up to a foot of rain fell overnight in southeastern Missouri, prompting more than 350 rescues from floodwaters overall. More than 20 million people across at least 14 states from Colorado to Pennsylvania are under flood watches through Saturday. The flash-flood threat is continuing into Sunday, extending from Tennessee to West Virginia. The threat has expanded significantly in Texas: a state of emergency has been declared covering nearly 60 counties, a flash flood emergency has been triggered in Central Texas, more than a foot of rain has fallen in parts of Texas in 24 hours leading to dozens of rescues, highways have been washed out, and motorists have been stranded. A tornado was spawned in San Antonio. Kerr County officials — site of last year's Camp Mystic disaster that killed 28 people — are in contact with summer camps now at risk. Forecasters warn of isolated totals of up to 15 inches possible. Camp Mystic operators have moved five lawsuits filed by families over last year's catastrophic flooding to federal court, citing bankruptcy. A heat dome is simultaneously driving triple-digit temperatures from Southern California to the Northeast, threatening record-breaking heat. Separately, days of torrential monsoon rain have triggered major flooding in Bangladesh, killing at least 51 people and leaving millions stranded in the south-east of the country, with food supply shortages reported. On the immigration enforcement front: a Venezuelan man (Jesús Manuel Arenas-Silva, 45) died in ICE custody in Georgia, becoming the 22nd such death this year. A 28-year-old man fleeing ICE agents in St. Augustine, Florida was struck and killed by a tractor-trailer, the third death in a week involving ICE encounters following fatal shootings of two men during vehicle stops in Maine and Texas six days apart. In response, ICE has suspended most vehicle stops.

clusters.state_of_play: China and North Korea are marking the 65th anniversary of their friendship treaty. North Korean Premier Pak Thae-song traveled to Beijing, met with Xi Jinping, and Kim Jong-un and Xi exchanged messages pledging deeper strategic cooperation. Separately, Kim Jong-un convened a rare military commission meeting where he denounced corruption in the military, announced plans to boost North Korea's nuclear force in quality and quantity, and ordered a radical expansion of espionage activities targeting South Korea. South Korea has separately voiced concern that North Korean actions along the DMZ constitute a breach of the 1953 armistice agreement. In a related development, China has put Chinese-born American seismologist Youlin Chen on trial after nearly two years of detention; Chen published US-funded research on detecting North Korean nuclear tests and worked as a US government contractor for the State Department and Air Force Research Lab. China's foreign ministry has rejected claims of 'wrongful detention' while not denying that Chen is imprisoned. Chen's wife Yufang Rong is publicly appealing to Trump to help bring him home. New reporting reveals that Trump made a direct personal appeal to Xi Jinping for Chen's release, which went unanswered. Separately, a major Iranian newspaper has published a threat of retaliation against German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, drawing concern from German politicians and a cautious response from the German government. In technology and finance developments: CXMT, China's leading memory chip maker and a linchpin of its AI ambitions, is planning a ~$10B IPO in Shanghai. Oracle is leading a bid to supply Japan with air-gapped top-secret cloud services, under US pressure on Tokyo to tighten data security. Japan's government bond market is selling off amid policy normalization and fiscal concerns, with some experts flagging renewed investor opportunity. Satellite images have revealed that China has constructed a full-scale replica of a US Navy destroyer in the Taklamakan Desert, suggesting active target practice or weapons testing against US naval hardware profiles. A US airstrike on Feb. 28 killed approximately 200 people, mostly schoolchildren, at the Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab, Iran; the Pentagon's investigation findings remain withheld, with Democratic senators led by Kirsten Gillibrand demanding release within one week, while Trump has shrugged off the incident and the US officially has not accepted responsibility. In London, Metropolitan Police are investigating Chinese embassy guards for allegedly brandishing cattle prods at protestors, while a High Court legal challenge has begun over China's plans for a large new embassy building. A new Pew Research Center survey finds that more countries around the world now favour China over the US, and that global confidence in Xi Jinping exceeds that in Donald Trump.

clusters.state_of_play: The US has launched fresh waves of strikes on Iran including daytime strikes, and has reimposed a naval blockade on all Iranian ports. US strikes have hit port cities of Bushehr and Bandar Abbas, as well as a 90-minute attack on Iran's Greater Tunb Island targeting cruise missile storage and launch sites. US attacks have killed dozens in Iran, pushing a fragile ceasefire closer to collapse. A Situation Room meeting was held to plan a wider offensive broader in scope than the current Strait of Hormuz campaign. Trump warned strikes would intensify next week if Iran does not cooperate in peace talks, while also calling off a previously announced 20% fee on Hormuz shipping, replacing it with investment and trade deals with Gulf Arab states. US strikes hit an Iranian army barracks, killing at least 7 troops and wounding more than 260 people across the country. Iran has threatened to halt all Middle East energy exports in response to the blockade. Iran claims to have destroyed the US Fifth Fleet command centre and targeted a US naval support base in Bahrain's capital, with sirens reported in Manama. Iran has also attacked Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan; Jordan shot down three Iranian missiles. Iran claims to have killed 3 US service members in Kuwait, while the official US death toll stands at 14. The US used sea drones in combat for the first time to strike an Iranian submarine and ship maintenance facility near the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude is above $87 per barrel. Dubai has announced plans to build a new port to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf states more broadly are exploring alternative routes. Former officials say a stable peace appears elusive and characterise the current Hormuz campaign as Trump's third major strategic shift in the Iran conflict. Separately, Ukraine has struck more than 100 Russian vessels in the Sea of Azov over nine days and has also struck 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Russia's Agriculture Ministry is actively seeking alternative shipping routes and denies the strikes will affect export capacity, though Russian oil at sea is near a year-high as Moscow struggles to sell its exports. Russian strikes on Odesa killed at least 3 people and wounded 3 others. Trump has said Putin is ready to make a deal to end the Ukraine war, though Russia has warned that Western troops enforcing any ceasefire would be treated as military targets. The EU and Ukraine have signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures, combining Ukraine's battlefield expertise with EU scale. Treasury Secretary Bessent has announced a Trump gold coin featuring the sitting president will go into production. In China, official data shows GDP grew 4.3% in Q2, the weakest quarterly growth since late 2022, driven by slow consumer demand despite a surge in exports. DeepSeek is weighing an IPO and considering raising new private funds after completing a first financing round that valued the company at $52 billion; Zhipu has separately embraced an AGI positioning. Hong Kong police raided two bookstores and arrested five people for allegedly selling seditious publications, underscoring the political changes that have eroded the territory's once-open publishing environment.

clusters.state_of_play: China and North Korea are marking the 65th anniversary of their friendship treaty. North Korean Premier Pak Thae-song traveled to Beijing, met with Xi Jinping, and Kim Jong-un and Xi exchanged messages pledging deeper strategic cooperation. Separately, Kim Jong-un convened a rare military commission meeting where he denounced corruption in the military, announced plans to boost North Korea's nuclear force in quality and quantity, and ordered a radical expansion of espionage activities targeting South Korea. South Korea has separately voiced concern that North Korean actions along the DMZ constitute a breach of the 1953 armistice agreement. In a related development, China has put Chinese-born American seismologist Youlin Chen on trial after nearly two years of detention; Chen published US-funded research on detecting North Korean nuclear tests and worked as a US government contractor for the State Department and Air Force Research Lab. China's foreign ministry has rejected claims of 'wrongful detention' while not denying that Chen is imprisoned. Chen's wife Yufang Rong is publicly appealing to Trump to help bring him home. New reporting reveals that Trump made a direct personal appeal to Xi Jinping for Chen's release, which went unanswered. Separately, a major Iranian newspaper has published a threat of retaliation against German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, drawing concern from German politicians and a cautious response from the German government. In technology and finance developments: CXMT, China's leading memory chip maker and a linchpin of its AI ambitions, is planning a ~$10B IPO in Shanghai. Oracle is leading a bid to supply Japan with air-gapped top-secret cloud services, under US pressure on Tokyo to tighten data security. Japan's government bond market is selling off amid policy normalization and fiscal concerns, with some experts flagging renewed investor opportunity. Satellite images have revealed that China has constructed a full-scale replica of a US Navy destroyer in the Taklamakan Desert, suggesting active target practice or weapons testing against US naval hardware profiles. A US airstrike on Feb. 28 killed approximately 200 people, mostly schoolchildren, at the Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab, Iran; the Pentagon's investigation findings remain withheld, with Democratic senators led by Kirsten Gillibrand demanding release within one week, while Trump has shrugged off the incident and the US officially has not accepted responsibility. In London, Metropolitan Police are investigating Chinese embassy guards for allegedly brandishing cattle prods at protestors, while a High Court legal challenge has begun over China's plans for a large new embassy building. A new Pew Research Center survey finds that more countries around the world now favour China over the US, and that global confidence in Xi Jinping exceeds that in Donald Trump.
